# From Solidity examples to Sauce

The protocols publish their own examples in Solidity: a contract you deploy, fund and then call.
Each example below is one of them ported to Sauce: one program, compiled for a chain and sent as
one transaction from your Pot, with nothing deployed. The protocol's contracts are named, never
written as addresses (`UniswapV3.SwapRouter`), each function of the Solidity contract is a
function of the program, and what it took as arguments `main` takes. The header of each program
says what changed and why, and gives the `sauce` command that runs it.

Every program here runs, not only compiles, before the package ships: through `sauce simulate`
and `sauce run` on Ethereum's state at a fixed block, against the protocols' deployed contracts,
with each result held to the protocol's own quotes and accounts.

A flash loan changes most. A lender pays first and then calls its borrower back to be repaid,
Uniswap's pool through `uniswapV3FlashCallback` and Aave's Pool through `executeOperation`, and
a Pot cannot be called back by a program. The flash a program has is its Router's: a swap whose
output arrives first, with a program run inside the swap's callback, before the pool is paid.
Uniswap's `PairFlash` is ported that way below; Aave's flash-loan receiver has no port, since
the same trade is that flash swap. Balancer's flash swap needs no callback at all: the Vault
settles a batch of swaps as a whole, so it ports as it is.

What a port saves is the contract, not its length: nothing is deployed, funded or upgraded, and
nothing holds an approval between transactions, since the program runs in your Pot and is gone.
Some ports come out shorter than their Solidity and some about as long, as the counts below show.
Lines are counted whole, and as code: neither blank nor only a comment. A Solidity count leaves
out the libraries and interfaces the example imports; a Sauce program imports nothing it does
not ship with.

## Uniswap V3: the swap examples

Ported from Uniswap/docs, [`content/examples/smart-contracts/SwapExamples.sol`](https://github.com/Uniswap/docs/blob/338d70983ac49911aecac02dd57b0a969c1ca61e/content/examples/smart-contracts/SwapExamples.sol): 163 lines of Solidity, 80 of them code. In Sauce, `uniswap-v3-swap-examples.sauce.ts`: 128 lines, 84 of them code.

```ts
// Uniswap's swap examples, ported: the four swaps of the `SwapExamples` contract in Uniswap's V3
// guides, through the chain's Uniswap V3 SwapRouter, as one program. `multihop` picks the route,
// DAI → WETH in the 0.3% pool or DAI → USDC → WETH; `exactOutput` picks the exact side, DAI sold
// or WETH bought. It returns what the router returns: the WETH bought, or with
// `exactOutput` the DAI spent.
//
// Ported from Uniswap/docs, content/examples/smart-contracts/SwapExamples.sol (163 lines, 80 of code):
// https://github.com/Uniswap/docs/blob/338d70983ac49911aecac02dd57b0a969c1ca61e/content/examples/smart-contracts/SwapExamples.sol
//
// What changes in Sauce: the contract pulled DAI from its caller and was deployed with the router's
// address; the program spends the Pot's DAI (send it to the Pot first) and names the router
// `UniswapV3.SwapRouter` and DAI `Maker.Dai`, the registry's names for them. Each Solidity function
// is a function here, with `msg.sender` as `recipient`. The original passes `amountOutMinimum: 0`
// and says to choose a safer value in production: `limit` is that value. It also takes both hops
// through 0.3% pools; DAI and USDC trade in the 0.01% pool now (the 0.3% one turns 1,000 DAI into
// about 116 USDC), so the path takes that hop at 0.01%.
//
//   sauce run uniswap-v3-swap-examples.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <multihop> <exactOutput> <amount> <limit> <recipient>
//
//   multihop: bool        false: DAI → WETH in one pool; true: DAI → USDC → WETH
//   exactOutput: bool     false: sell exactly `amount` DAI; true: buy exactly `amount` WETH
//   amount: Uint256       the DAI to sell, or the WETH to buy, in smallest units (18 decimals):
//                         1000000000000000000000 is 1,000 DAI
//   limit: Uint256        the least WETH to accept for `amount` DAI, or with `exactOutput` the most
//                         DAI to spend for `amount` WETH, in smallest units; what is not spent
//                         stays in the Pot
//   recipient: Address    who receives the WETH
//
// On Ethereum, 1,000 DAI sold for at least 0.25 WETH in the 0.3% pool:
//
//   sauce run uniswap-v3-swap-examples.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args false false 1000000000000000000000 250000000000000000 <recipient>

const POOL_FEE = 3000;
const STABLE_FEE = 100;

// A path the router reads: each token's 20 bytes, with the fee of the pool between two in 3.
function path(a: Address, feeAB: Uint256, b: Address, feeBC: Uint256, c: Address): bytes {
  return a
    .toBytesBe(20)
    .concat(feeAB.toBytesBe(3), b.toBytesBe(20), feeBC.toBytesBe(3), c.toBytesBe(20));
}

function swapExactInputSingle(amountIn: Uint256, minOut: Uint256, recipient: Address): Uint256 {
  require(UniswapV3.SwapRouter && Maker.Dai);
  approve(Maker.Dai, UniswapV3.SwapRouter, amountIn);
  return UniswapV3.SwapRouter.exactInputSingle({
    tokenIn: Maker.Dai,
    tokenOut: WETH,
    fee: POOL_FEE,
    recipient,
    deadline: ctx.timestamp(),
    amountIn,
    amountOutMinimum: minOut,
    sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0,
  });
}

function swapExactOutputSingle(amountOut: Uint256, maxIn: Uint256, recipient: Address): Uint256 {
  require(UniswapV3.SwapRouter && Maker.Dai);
  approve(Maker.Dai, UniswapV3.SwapRouter, maxIn);
  const amountIn = UniswapV3.SwapRouter.exactOutputSingle({
    tokenIn: Maker.Dai,
    tokenOut: WETH,
    fee: POOL_FEE,
    recipient,
    deadline: ctx.timestamp(),
    amountOut,
    amountInMaximum: maxIn,
    sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0,
  });
  // The router took less than the maximum: withdraw the allowance it did not use, as the
  // original does. The DAI it did not take is still the Pot's.
  if (amountIn < maxIn) {
    approve(Maker.Dai, UniswapV3.SwapRouter, 0);
  }
  return amountIn;
}

function swapExactInputMultihop(amountIn: Uint256, minOut: Uint256, recipient: Address): Uint256 {
  require(UniswapV3.SwapRouter && Maker.Dai);
  approve(Maker.Dai, UniswapV3.SwapRouter, amountIn);
  return UniswapV3.SwapRouter.exactInput({
    path: path(Maker.Dai, STABLE_FEE, USDC, POOL_FEE, WETH),
    recipient,
    deadline: ctx.timestamp(),
    amountIn,
    amountOutMinimum: minOut,
  });
}

function swapExactOutputMultihop(amountOut: Uint256, maxIn: Uint256, recipient: Address): Uint256 {
  require(UniswapV3.SwapRouter && Maker.Dai);
  approve(Maker.Dai, UniswapV3.SwapRouter, maxIn);
  // An exact-output path runs backwards, from the token bought to the token paid.
  const amountIn = UniswapV3.SwapRouter.exactOutput({
    path: path(WETH, POOL_FEE, USDC, STABLE_FEE, Maker.Dai),
    recipient,
    deadline: ctx.timestamp(),
    amountOut,
    amountInMaximum: maxIn,
  });
  if (amountIn < maxIn) {
    approve(Maker.Dai, UniswapV3.SwapRouter, 0);
  }
  return amountIn;
}

function main(
  multihop: bool,
  exactOutput: bool,
  amount: Uint256,
  limit: Uint256,
  recipient: Address,
): Uint256 {
  require(Maker.Dai);
  const spendable = balanceOf(Maker.Dai, ctx.self());
  require(spendable >= (exactOutput ? limit : amount), "the DAI to spend is not in the Pot");
  if (multihop) {
    return exactOutput
      ? swapExactOutputMultihop(amount, limit, recipient)
      : swapExactInputMultihop(amount, limit, recipient);
  }
  return exactOutput
    ? swapExactOutputSingle(amount, limit, recipient)
    : swapExactInputSingle(amount, limit, recipient);
}
```

## Uniswap V3: a flash, as a flash swap

Ported from Uniswap/v3-periphery, [`contracts/examples/PairFlash.sol`](https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-periphery/blob/0411d43779d01f4e82cfc31aea00fd6011b3756d/contracts/examples/PairFlash.sol): 149 lines of Solidity, 109 of them code. In Sauce, `uniswap-v3-pair-flash.sauce.ts`: 75 lines, 31 of them code.

```ts
// Uniswap's flash example, ported: `PairFlash` borrows from one Uniswap V3 pool, trades the loan
// through the pair's other pools, repays the loan with its fee and pays what is left to the caller.
// Here the loan is a flash swap: `amountIn` of `tokenIn` is sold in the `borrowFee` pool, and its
// `tokenOut` is in the Pot before anything is paid; a program then sells that `tokenOut` back in the
// `repayFee` pool for at least `amountIn`; the borrow pool is paid `amountIn` out of it, and the rest
// is the profit, sent to `payer` and returned. Nothing the Pot already held is spent: a trade that
// cannot repay reverts the whole transaction, as PairFlash's does.
//
// Ported from Uniswap/v3-periphery, contracts/examples/PairFlash.sol (149 lines, 109 of code):
// https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-periphery/blob/0411d43779d01f4e82cfc31aea00fd6011b3756d/contracts/examples/PairFlash.sol
//
// What changes in Sauce: a pool's `flash` pays the borrower and then calls it back
// (`uniswapV3FlashCallback`) to be repaid, and a Pot cannot be called back by a program: its fallback
// runs its Router. The Router's `flash(callback, swap)` is Sauce's flash: it runs one swap, whose
// pool sends the output first, runs `callback` inside the pool's callback, and pays the pool after
// it. `program()` compiles the callback, a closure that reads the program's own values, and
// SauceRouterFlash.json beside this file declares `flash`. So the loan is one token, sold rather
// than lent, and its fee is the borrow pool's swap fee; PairFlash's second loan and third pool are
// the same trade the other way round.
//
//   sauce run uniswap-v3-pair-flash.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <tokenIn> <tokenOut> <borrowFee> <amountIn> <repayFee> <payer>
//
//   tokenIn: Address      the token the borrow pool is paid in, after the callback
//   tokenOut: Address     the token the borrow pool sends first
//   borrowFee: Uint256    the borrow pool's fee tier, in millionths: 500 is 0.05%
//   amountIn: Uint256     how much `tokenIn` the borrow pool is paid, in its smallest units:
//                         1000000000000000000 is 1 WETH (18 decimals)
//   repayFee: Uint256     the fee tier of the pool the borrowed `tokenOut` is sold back in
//   payer: Address        who receives the profit, in `tokenIn`
//
// On Ethereum, 1 WETH's worth of USDC borrowed from the 0.05% pool and sold back for WETH in the
// 0.3% pool:
//
//   sauce run uniswap-v3-pair-flash.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 \
//     500 1000000000000000000 3000 <payer>
import { uniswapV3 } from "@sauce/router";
import SauceRouterFlash from "./SauceRouterFlash.json";

function main(
  tokenIn: Address,
  tokenOut: Address,
  borrowFee: Uint256,
  amountIn: Uint256,
  repayFee: Uint256,
  payer: Address,
): Uint256 {
  require(UniswapV3.Factory);
  const self = ctx.self();
  const borrowPool = UniswapV3.Factory.getPool(tokenIn, tokenOut, borrowFee);
  const repayPool = UniswapV3.Factory.getPool(tokenIn, tokenOut, repayFee);
  require(borrowPool != 0 && repayPool != 0, "no pool at those fee tiers");
  const inBefore = Token(tokenIn).balanceOf(self);
  const outBefore = Token(tokenOut).balanceOf(self);

  // The callback: the borrow pool has sent `tokenOut` and is not paid yet. Sell what it sent back
  // for at least what it is owed, into the Pot, which pays it.
  const repay = program(() => {
    const received = Token(tokenOut).balanceOf(self) - outBefore;
    uniswapV3(repayPool, tokenOut, tokenIn, received, 0, amountIn, self);
  }, chainId);
  // The swap the Router runs around it, as the calldata of its own `swapV3`.
  const swapV3 = (crypto.keccak256("swapV3(address,address,bool,uint256,uint160,address)") >> 224)
    .toBytesBe(4)
    .concat(abi.encode(borrowPool, tokenIn, tokenIn < tokenOut, amountIn, 0, self));
  SauceRouterFlash.at(self).flash(repay.code.concat(repay.args), swapV3);

  // What the repayment left of `tokenIn`, beyond what the Pot held: the profit.
  const profit = Token(tokenIn).balanceOf(self) - inBefore;
  if (profit > 0) {
    Token(tokenIn).transfer(payer, profit);
  }
  return profit;
}
```

## Uniswap V3: the liquidity examples

Ported from Uniswap/docs, [`content/examples/smart-contracts/LiquidityExamples.sol`](https://github.com/Uniswap/docs/blob/338d70983ac49911aecac02dd57b0a969c1ca61e/content/examples/smart-contracts/LiquidityExamples.sol): 243 lines of Solidity, 157 of them code. In Sauce, `uniswap-v3-liquidity-examples.sauce.ts`: 162 lines, 116 of them code.

```ts
// Uniswap's liquidity examples, ported: the `LiquidityExamples` contract of Uniswap's V3 guides
// keeps a DAI/USDC position's NFT for its owner and mints it, collects its fees, takes half its
// liquidity out, adds to it and hands the NFT back. Here the Pot is that contract: the position is
// minted to the Pot, and only its owner cooks it. `step` picks the function, and each returns the
// position's `tokenId`, the liquidity it added or removed, and the DAI and USDC that moved.
//
// Ported from Uniswap/docs, content/examples/smart-contracts/LiquidityExamples.sol (243 lines, 157 of code):
// https://github.com/Uniswap/docs/blob/338d70983ac49911aecac02dd57b0a969c1ca61e/content/examples/smart-contracts/LiquidityExamples.sol
//
// What changes in Sauce: the contract recorded each deposit's owner, because anyone could call it;
// a Pot is cooked by its owner alone, so there is no record and no owner check, and `owner` is
// where the tokens and the NFT go. It pulled the tokens from its caller and refunded what the
// position did not take; the Pot's tokens stay in the Pot. Its full range was TickMath's, which no
// 0.3% pool accepts (a tick must be a multiple of the tier's spacing, 60): here it is that range
// rounded in. Its `decreaseLiquidityInHalf` sent the owner tokens the position had only credited,
// not paid: here it collects them first. Position reads and the NFT's transfer are in
// UniswapV3Positions.json beside this file, which the registry's ABI for the position manager
// leaves out.
//
//   sauce run uniswap-v3-liquidity-examples.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <step> <tokenId> <amount0> <amount1> <owner>
//
//   step: Uint256      0 mint a position, 1 collect all its fees, 2 take half its liquidity out,
//                      3 add to it, 4 hand its NFT to `owner`
//   tokenId: Uint256   the position (0 to mint one)
//   amount0: Uint256   the DAI to mint or add with, in its smallest units (18 decimals):
//                      1000000000000000000000 is 1,000 DAI
//   amount1: Uint256   the USDC to mint or add with, in its smallest units (6 decimals):
//                      1000000000 is 1,000 USDC
//   owner: Address     who receives the fees, the liquidity taken out and the NFT
//
// On Ethereum, a full-range position minted with up to 1,000 DAI and 1,000 USDC:
//
//   sauce run uniswap-v3-liquidity-examples.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args 0 0 1000000000000000000000 1000000000 <owner>
import UniswapV3Positions from "./UniswapV3Positions.json";

const POOL_FEE = 3000;
// TickMath's MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK, rounded in to the 0.3% tier's tick spacing of 60.
const MIN_TICK = -887220;
const MAX_TICK = 887220;
const MAX_UINT128 = 2 ** 128 - 1;

interface Moved {
  tokenId: Uint256;
  liquidity: Uint256;
  amount0: Uint256;
  amount1: Uint256;
}

function mintNewPosition(amount0ToMint: Uint256, amount1ToMint: Uint256): Moved {
  require(UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager && Maker.Dai);
  const manager = UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager;
  approve(Maker.Dai, manager, amount0ToMint);
  USDC.approve(manager, amount1ToMint);
  const [tokenId, liquidity, amount0, amount1] = manager.mint({
    token0: Maker.Dai,
    token1: USDC,
    fee: POOL_FEE,
    tickLower: MIN_TICK,
    tickUpper: MAX_TICK,
    amount0Desired: amount0ToMint,
    amount1Desired: amount1ToMint,
    amount0Min: 0,
    amount1Min: 0,
    recipient: ctx.self(),
    deadline: ctx.timestamp(),
  });
  // What the position did not take stays in the Pot; the allowance for it does not stand.
  if (amount0 < amount0ToMint) {
    approve(Maker.Dai, manager, 0);
  }
  if (amount1 < amount1ToMint) {
    USDC.approve(manager, 0);
  }
  return { tokenId, liquidity, amount0, amount1 };
}

function collectAllFees(tokenId: Uint256, owner: Address): Moved {
  require(UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager);
  const [amount0, amount1] = UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager.collect({
    tokenId,
    recipient: owner,
    amount0Max: MAX_UINT128,
    amount1Max: MAX_UINT128,
  });
  return { tokenId, liquidity: 0, amount0, amount1 };
}

function decreaseLiquidityInHalf(tokenId: Uint256, owner: Address): Moved {
  require(UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager);
  const manager = UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager;
  const position = UniswapV3Positions.at(manager).positions(tokenId);
  const halfLiquidity = position.liquidity / 2;
  const [amount0, amount1] = manager.decreaseLiquidity({
    tokenId,
    liquidity: halfLiquidity,
    amount0Min: 0,
    amount1Min: 0,
    deadline: ctx.timestamp(),
  });
  // Taking liquidity out credits the position; collecting pays the credit to `owner`.
  manager.collect({ tokenId, recipient: owner, amount0Max: amount0, amount1Max: amount1 });
  return { tokenId, liquidity: halfLiquidity, amount0, amount1 };
}

function increaseLiquidityCurrentRange(
  tokenId: Uint256,
  amountAdd0: Uint256,
  amountAdd1: Uint256,
): Moved {
  require(UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager);
  const manager = UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager;
  const position = UniswapV3Positions.at(manager).positions(tokenId);
  approve(position.token0, manager, amountAdd0);
  approve(position.token1, manager, amountAdd1);
  const [liquidity, amount0, amount1] = manager.increaseLiquidity({
    tokenId,
    amount0Desired: amountAdd0,
    amount1Desired: amountAdd1,
    amount0Min: 0,
    amount1Min: 0,
    deadline: ctx.timestamp(),
  });
  if (amount0 < amountAdd0) {
    approve(position.token0, manager, 0);
  }
  if (amount1 < amountAdd1) {
    approve(position.token1, manager, 0);
  }
  return { tokenId, liquidity, amount0, amount1 };
}

function retrieveNFT(tokenId: Uint256, owner: Address): Moved {
  require(UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager);
  const manager = UniswapV3.NonfungiblePositionManager;
  UniswapV3Positions.at(manager).safeTransferFrom(ctx.self(), owner, tokenId);
  return { tokenId, liquidity: 0, amount0: 0, amount1: 0 };
}

function main(
  step: Uint256,
  tokenId: Uint256,
  amount0: Uint256,
  amount1: Uint256,
  owner: Address,
): Moved {
  if (step == 0) {
    return mintNewPosition(amount0, amount1);
  }
  if (step == 1) {
    return collectAllFees(tokenId, owner);
  }
  if (step == 2) {
    return decreaseLiquidityInHalf(tokenId, owner);
  }
  if (step == 3) {
    return increaseLiquidityCurrentRange(tokenId, amount0, amount1);
  }
  require(step == 4, "step is 0 to 4");
  return retrieveNFT(tokenId, owner);
}
```

## Aave V3: credit delegation

Ported from aave/code-examples-protocol, [`V2/Credit Delegation/MyV2CreditDelegation.sol`](https://github.com/aave/code-examples-protocol/blob/c343d266d04f210e1de9a7f008fdbc8ad63e5c22/V2/Credit%20Delegation/MyV2CreditDelegation.sol): 83 lines of Solidity, 33 of them code. In Sauce, `aave-v3-credit-delegation.sauce.ts`: 81 lines, 42 of them code.

```ts
// Aave's credit delegation example, ported to Aave V3: `MyV2CreditDelegation` supplies collateral to
// Aave, lets one borrower borrow against it, repays that borrower's debt and takes the collateral
// back. Here the Pot is the delegator: the collateral is the Pot's, the debt the borrower runs up is
// the Pot's, and only its owner cooks it. `step` picks the function, and each returns the amount it
// moved or allowed.
//
// Ported from aave/code-examples-protocol, V2/Credit Delegation/MyV2CreditDelegation.sol (83 lines, 33 of code):
// https://github.com/aave/code-examples-protocol/blob/c343d266d04f210e1de9a7f008fdbc8ad63e5c22/V2/Credit%20Delegation/MyV2CreditDelegation.sol
//
// What changes in Sauce: Aave's own example targets its second version, and this the third, whose
// Pool is the registry's `AaveV3.Pool`: `deposit` is `supply`, and the debt is variable, since the
// third version takes no new stable-rate debt. The contract pulled tokens from its caller when asked
// to (`isPull`); the Pot's tokens are already the Pot's. It found the debt and aTokens through
// Aave's data provider, a Kovan address; the Pool names them itself, in AaveV3Delegation.json beside
// this file with the debt token's `approveDelegation`, which the registry's ABI leaves out. And it
// withdrew to the contract's deployer; `account` is who receives the collateral.
//
//   sauce run aave-v3-credit-delegation.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <step> <asset> <amount> <account>
//
//   step: Uint256      0 supply `amount` of `asset` as collateral, 1 let `account` borrow up to
//                      `amount` of `asset` against it, 2 repay up to `amount` of the debt in `asset`,
//                      3 withdraw all the `asset` collateral to `account`
//   asset: Address     the token supplied, delegated, repaid or withdrawn
//   amount: Uint256    how much, in the token's smallest units: 1000000000 is 1,000 USDC (6 decimals)
//   account: Address   the borrower (step 1), or who receives the collateral (step 3)
//
// On Ethereum, a borrower allowed up to 1,000 USDC against the Pot's collateral:
//
//   sauce run aave-v3-credit-delegation.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args 1 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 1000000000 <borrower>
import AaveV3Delegation from "./AaveV3Delegation.json";

// The variable rate, as Aave's `interestRateMode` names it.
const VARIABLE = 2;

function depositCollateral(asset: Address, amount: Uint256): Uint256 {
  require(AaveV3.Pool);
  approve(asset, AaveV3.Pool, amount);
  AaveV3.Pool.supply(asset, amount, ctx.self(), 0);
  return amount;
}

function approveBorrower(borrower: Address, amount: Uint256, asset: Address): Uint256 {
  require(AaveV3.Pool);
  const debtToken = AaveV3Delegation.at(AaveV3.Pool).getReserveVariableDebtToken(asset);
  AaveV3Delegation.at(debtToken).approveDelegation(borrower, amount);
  return amount;
}

function repayBorrower(amount: Uint256, asset: Address): Uint256 {
  require(AaveV3.Pool);
  approve(asset, AaveV3.Pool, amount);
  const repaid = AaveV3.Pool.repay(asset, amount, VARIABLE, ctx.self());
  // A repayment above the debt pays the debt: the allowance for the rest does not stand.
  if (repaid < amount) {
    approve(asset, AaveV3.Pool, 0);
  }
  return repaid;
}

function withdrawCollateral(asset: Address, to: Address): Uint256 {
  require(AaveV3.Pool);
  const aToken = AaveV3Delegation.at(AaveV3.Pool).getReserveAToken(asset);
  const assetBalance = Token(aToken).balanceOf(ctx.self());
  return AaveV3.Pool.withdraw(asset, assetBalance, to);
}

function main(step: Uint256, asset: Address, amount: Uint256, account: Address): Uint256 {
  if (step == 0) {
    return depositCollateral(asset, amount);
  }
  if (step == 1) {
    return approveBorrower(account, amount, asset);
  }
  if (step == 2) {
    return repayBorrower(amount, asset);
  }
  require(step == 3, "step is 0 to 3");
  return withdrawCollateral(asset, account);
}
```

## Compound III: MyContract

Ported from compound-developers/compound-3-developer-faq, [`contracts/MyContract.sol`](https://github.com/compound-developers/compound-3-developer-faq/blob/d43332f99208bbc454929fe5cdef2aecbbccf979/contracts/MyContract.sol): 337 lines of Solidity, 225 of them code. In Sauce, `compound-v3-my-contract.sauce.ts`: 203 lines, 141 of them code.

```ts
// Compound's own example, ported: `MyContract` of the Compound III developer FAQ supplies to a
// Comet market, withdraws from it (a borrow, once the base token runs out), repays a whole borrow
// and claims COMP, and reads what a developer asks of the market: the supply and borrow APRs, the
// reward APRs, what an account can still borrow, an asset's collateral factors and price, the
// rewards owed and the market's TVL. Here every cook does its `step` (0 does nothing) and returns
// those reads for the Pot, so `sauce simulate` with step 0 is the read-only call.
//
// Ported from compound-developers/compound-3-developer-faq, contracts/MyContract.sol (337 lines, 225 of code):
// https://github.com/compound-developers/compound-3-developer-faq/blob/d43332f99208bbc454929fe5cdef2aecbbccf979/contracts/MyContract.sol
//
// What changes in Sauce: the contract was deployed for one Comet and its views read that Comet;
// `comet` is a `main` input, and the Pot is the account. Its `presentValue` cast a negative
// principal to unsigned before scaling it, which reads a borrower's debt as a vast supply: here the
// principal's sign is taken first, as Comet's own does, and the debt kept apart from the collateral
// until the end, since SauceScript's arithmetic is unsigned. It divided each amount at its price by
// the price's scale, 1e8, which leaves WETH in 18 decimals beside USDC in 6: each is divided by its
// own token's scale here (`baseScale`, an asset's `scale`), so they sum in USD with 8 decimals.
// Its `getAllAssetInfos` logged every asset's settings for a developer to read; a simulation
// returns what a program reads instead, so it is left out. The Comet and CometRewards functions
// are in Comet.json beside this file, since the registry's ABI declares only the Comet's supply
// and withdraw paths and balances.
//
//   sauce run compound-v3-my-contract.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <step> <comet> <asset> <amount> <rewards> <rewardFeed>
//
//   step: Uint256         0 nothing, 1 supply `amount` of `asset`, 2 withdraw `amount` of `asset`
//                         (of the base token, a borrow past what is supplied), 3 repay the whole
//                         borrow, 4 claim the Pot's rewards
//   comet: Address        the Comet market, `CompoundV3.CUSDCv3` on Ethereum
//   asset: Address        the token supplied or withdrawn, and whose factors and price are read
//   amount: Uint256       how much, in the token's smallest units: 1000000000 is 1,000 USDC
//   rewards: Address      the market's CometRewards contract, which owes and pays COMP: the one
//                         Compound's documentation lists for the chain
//   rewardFeed: Address   the reward token's price feed, as the Comet prices it: on the USDC
//                         market, the `priceFeed` of COMP's `getAssetInfoByAddress`
//
// On Ethereum, the USDC market read with nothing changed:
//
//   sauce simulate compound-v3-my-contract.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --owner <owner> \
//     --args 0 0xc3d688B66703497DAA19211EEdff47f25384cdc3 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 \
//     0 <rewards> <rewardFeed>
import Comet from "./Comet.json";

const DAYS_PER_YEAR = 365;
const SECONDS_PER_DAY = 60 * 60 * 24;
const SECONDS_PER_YEAR = SECONDS_PER_DAY * DAYS_PER_YEAR;
const MAX_UINT = ~0;

interface Market {
  // What the step supplied, withdrew, repaid or claimed: 0 for step 0.
  moved: Uint256;
  supplyApr: Uint256;
  borrowApr: Uint256;
  rewardAprForSupplyBase: Uint256;
  rewardAprForBorrowBase: Uint256;
  // What the Pot can still borrow, in USD with 8 decimals: a signed number, negative past its limit.
  borrowable: Uint256;
  borrowCollateralFactor: Uint256;
  liquidateCollateralFactor: Uint256;
  price: Uint256;
  rewardsOwed: Uint256;
  tvl: Uint256;
}

function supply(comet: Address, asset: Address, amount: Uint256): Uint256 {
  approve(asset, comet, amount);
  Comet.at(comet).supply(asset, amount);
  return amount;
}

function withdraw(comet: Address, asset: Address, amount: Uint256): Uint256 {
  Comet.at(comet).withdraw(asset, amount);
  return amount;
}

function repayFullBorrow(comet: Address): Uint256 {
  const baseAsset = Comet.at(comet).baseToken();
  const before = Token(baseAsset).balanceOf(ctx.self());
  // Supplying the maximum repays exactly the borrow: the allowance for the rest goes back to zero.
  approve(baseAsset, comet, MAX_UINT);
  Comet.at(comet).supply(baseAsset, MAX_UINT);
  approve(baseAsset, comet, 0);
  return before - Token(baseAsset).balanceOf(ctx.self());
}

function claimCometRewards(comet: Address, rewards: Address): Uint256 {
  const owed = Comet.at(rewards).getRewardOwed(comet, ctx.self());
  Comet.at(rewards).claim(comet, ctx.self(), true);
  return owed.owed;
}

function getSupplyApr(comet: Address): Uint256 {
  const utilization = Comet.at(comet).getUtilization();
  return Comet.at(comet).getSupplyRate(utilization) * SECONDS_PER_YEAR * 100;
}

function getBorrowApr(comet: Address): Uint256 {
  const utilization = Comet.at(comet).getUtilization();
  return Comet.at(comet).getBorrowRate(utilization) * SECONDS_PER_YEAR * 100;
}

// The reward a base supplier (`borrow` false) or borrower earns a year, per dollar, scaled by 1e18.
function getRewardApr(comet: Address, rewardTokenPriceFeed: Address, borrow: bool): Uint256 {
  const market = Comet.at(comet);
  const rewardTokenPriceInUsd = market.getPrice(rewardTokenPriceFeed);
  const usdcPriceInUsd = market.getPrice(market.baseTokenPriceFeed());
  const total = borrow ? market.totalBorrow() : market.totalSupply();
  const speed = borrow ? market.baseTrackingBorrowSpeed() : market.baseTrackingSupplySpeed();
  const rewardPerDay = speed * SECONDS_PER_DAY * (market.baseIndexScale() / market.baseScale());
  return ((rewardTokenPriceInUsd * rewardPerDay) / (total * usdcPriceInUsd)) * DAYS_PER_YEAR;
}

function getBorrowableAmount(comet: Address, account: Address): Uint256 {
  const market = Comet.at(comet);
  const user = market.userBasic(account);
  const totals = market.totalsBasic();
  const scale = market.baseIndexScale();
  const baseScale = market.baseScale();
  const basePrice = market.getPrice(market.baseTokenPriceFeed());
  // The base principal at the present index: a supply grows by the supply index, a borrow by the
  // borrow index. SauceScript's arithmetic is unsigned, so the two are kept apart until the end.
  let supplied = 0;
  let borrowed = 0;
  if (Math.sGte(user.principal, 0)) {
    supplied = (user.principal * totals.baseSupplyIndex) / scale;
  } else {
    borrowed = (-user.principal * totals.baseBorrowIndex) / scale;
  }
  // Every amount in USD with 8 decimals, as the Comet prices it: an amount of a token at its price
  // (8 decimals) over that token's own scale.
  let liquidity = (supplied * basePrice) / baseScale;
  for (let i = 0; i < market.numAssets(); i += 1) {
    if (((user.assetsIn >> i) & 1) == 1) {
      const asset = market.getAssetInfo(i);
      const balance = market.userCollateral(account, asset.asset).balance;
      const amount = (balance * market.getPrice(asset.priceFeed)) / asset.scale;
      liquidity += (amount * asset.borrowCollateralFactor) / 10 ** 18;
    }
  }
  const debt = (borrowed * basePrice) / baseScale;
  return liquidity >= debt ? liquidity - debt : -(debt - liquidity);
}

function getTvl(comet: Address): Uint256 {
  const market = Comet.at(comet);
  const baseScale = 10 ** Comet.at(comet).decimals();
  const basePrice = market.getPrice(market.baseTokenPriceFeed());
  let tvlUsd = (market.totalSupply() * basePrice) / baseScale;
  for (let i = 0; i < market.numAssets(); i += 1) {
    const asset = market.getAssetInfo(i);
    const totals = market.totalsCollateral(asset.asset);
    const scale = 10 ** Comet.at(asset.asset).decimals();
    tvlUsd += (totals.totalSupplyAsset * market.getPrice(asset.priceFeed)) / scale;
  }
  return tvlUsd;
}

function main(
  step: Uint256,
  comet: Address,
  asset: Address,
  amount: Uint256,
  rewards: Address,
  rewardFeed: Address,
): Market {
  require(step <= 4, "step is 0 to 4");
  let moved = 0;
  if (step == 1) {
    moved = supply(comet, asset, amount);
  }
  if (step == 2) {
    moved = withdraw(comet, asset, amount);
  }
  if (step == 3) {
    moved = repayFullBorrow(comet);
  }
  if (step == 4) {
    moved = claimCometRewards(comet, rewards);
  }
  // The base token is no collateral: it has no factors, and the market prices it by its own feed.
  let borrowCollateralFactor = 0;
  let liquidateCollateralFactor = 0;
  let feed = Comet.at(comet).baseTokenPriceFeed();
  if (asset != Comet.at(comet).baseToken()) {
    const info = Comet.at(comet).getAssetInfoByAddress(asset);
    borrowCollateralFactor = info.borrowCollateralFactor;
    liquidateCollateralFactor = info.liquidateCollateralFactor;
    feed = info.priceFeed;
  }
  return {
    moved,
    supplyApr: getSupplyApr(comet),
    borrowApr: getBorrowApr(comet),
    rewardAprForSupplyBase: getRewardApr(comet, rewardFeed, false),
    rewardAprForBorrowBase: getRewardApr(comet, rewardFeed, true),
    borrowable: getBorrowableAmount(comet, ctx.self()),
    borrowCollateralFactor,
    liquidateCollateralFactor,
    price: Comet.at(comet).getPrice(feed),
    rewardsOwed: Comet.at(rewards).getRewardOwed(comet, ctx.self()).owed,
    tvl: getTvl(comet),
  };
}
```

## Morpho Blue: the snippets

Ported from morpho-org/morpho-blue-snippets, [`src/morpho-blue/MorphoBlueSnippets.sol`](https://github.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue-snippets/blob/43568fd8626a2f44dc49e5ac7040ec6dc7ee67c3/src/morpho-blue/MorphoBlueSnippets.sol): 380 lines of Solidity, 219 of them code. In Sauce, `morpho-blue-snippets.sauce.ts`: 256 lines, 197 of them code.

```ts
// Morpho's snippets, ported: `MorphoBlueSnippets` is Morpho's catalogue of how to use one Morpho
// Blue market, each snippet a function: supply, supply collateral, withdraw it, withdraw an amount,
// half or all of a supply, borrow, repay an amount, half or all of a debt, and the views a position
// needs (the supply and borrow APYs, a user's supply, debt and collateral, the market's totals, the
// health factor). Here the Pot is the user: `step` picks a snippet (0 none), and every cook returns
// what it moved and those views for the Pot.
//
// Ported from morpho-org/morpho-blue-snippets, src/morpho-blue/MorphoBlueSnippets.sol (380 lines, 219 of code):
// https://github.com/morpho-org/morpho-blue-snippets/blob/43568fd8626a2f44dc49e5ac7040ec6dc7ee67c3/src/morpho-blue/MorphoBlueSnippets.sol
//
// What changes in Sauce: the snippets act for their caller, who must authorize the contract on
// Morpho, and pull its tokens; the Pot acts for itself, and `receiver` is where withdrawals and
// borrows go. They take the market's parameters; the program takes its id and reads them from
// Morpho, which is what `marketParams.id()` names. Their views compute in view-only math the
// interest accrued since the market was last touched (MorphoBalancesLib); a program runs as a
// transaction, even under `sauce simulate`, so it accrues the interest (`accrueInterest`) and reads
// the market. They approve the maximum and leave it standing; the program approves what each call
// spends. A user's collateral is read with `position`, not by its storage slot. Morpho's reads,
// the IRM's rate and the oracle's price are in MorphoBlueReads.json beside this file.
//
//   sauce run morpho-blue-snippets.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <step> <id> <amount> <receiver>
//
//   step: Uint256       0 none; 1 supply, 2 supply collateral, 3 withdraw collateral; 4 withdraw
//                       `amount`, 5 half, 6 all, 7 `amount` or all; 8 borrow; 9 repay `amount`,
//                       10 half, 11 all, 12 `amount` or all
//   id: Uint256         the market's id, as Morpho names it (a hash of its parameters)
//   amount: Uint256     how much of the loan or collateral token, in its smallest units:
//                       1000000000 is 1,000 USDC (6 decimals)
//   receiver: Address   who receives what a withdrawal or a borrow pays out
//
// On Ethereum, the USDC market with WETH collateral at an 86% LLTV, read with nothing changed:
//
//   sauce simulate morpho-blue-snippets.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --owner <owner> \
//     --args 0 0x94b823e6bd8ea533b4e33fbc307faea0b307301bc48763acc4d4aa4def7636cd 0 <receiver>
import MorphoReads from "./MorphoBlueReads.json";

const WAD = 10 ** 18;
const VIRTUAL_SHARES = 10 ** 6;
const VIRTUAL_ASSETS = 1;
const ORACLE_PRICE_SCALE = 10 ** 36;
const YEAR = 365 * 24 * 60 * 60;

// What a snippet supplied, withdrew, borrowed or repaid: assets, and shares where it moved shares.
interface Moved {
  assets: Uint256;
  shares: Uint256;
}

interface Snippet {
  // What the step's snippet moved.
  assets: Uint256;
  shares: Uint256;
  supplyApy: Uint256;
  borrowApy: Uint256;
  supplied: Uint256;
  borrowed: Uint256;
  collateral: Uint256;
  totalSupply: Uint256;
  totalBorrow: Uint256;
  healthFactor: Uint256;
}

// Morpho's share math (SharesMathLib): virtual shares and assets keep a market's first deposit
// from setting its price.
function toAssetsDown(shares: Uint256, totalAssets: Uint256, totalShares: Uint256): Uint256 {
  return Math.mulDiv(shares, totalAssets + VIRTUAL_ASSETS, totalShares + VIRTUAL_SHARES);
}

function toAssetsUp(shares: Uint256, totalAssets: Uint256, totalShares: Uint256): Uint256 {
  const d = totalShares + VIRTUAL_SHARES;
  return (shares * (totalAssets + VIRTUAL_ASSETS) + (d - 1)) / d;
}

// e^(x·n) - 1, to three terms (MathLib's wTaylorCompounded): a per-second rate compounded.
function wTaylorCompounded(x: Uint256, n: Uint256): Uint256 {
  const firstTerm = x * n;
  const secondTerm = Math.mulDiv(firstTerm, firstTerm, 2 * WAD);
  const thirdTerm = Math.mulDiv(secondTerm, firstTerm, 3 * WAD);
  return firstTerm + secondTerm + thirdTerm;
}

function supply(id: Uint256, amount: Uint256): Moved {
  require(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const params = MorphoReads.at(MorphoBlue.Morpho).idToMarketParams(id);
  approve(params.loanToken, MorphoBlue.Morpho, amount);
  const [assets, shares] = MorphoBlue.Morpho.supply(params, amount, 0, ctx.self(), hex``);
  return { assets: assets, shares: shares };
}

function supplyCollateral(id: Uint256, amount: Uint256): Moved {
  require(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const params = MorphoReads.at(MorphoBlue.Morpho).idToMarketParams(id);
  approve(params.collateralToken, MorphoBlue.Morpho, amount);
  MorphoBlue.Morpho.supplyCollateral(params, amount, ctx.self(), hex``);
  return { assets: amount, shares: 0 };
}

function withdrawCollateral(id: Uint256, amount: Uint256, receiver: Address): Moved {
  require(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const params = MorphoReads.at(MorphoBlue.Morpho).idToMarketParams(id);
  MorphoBlue.Morpho.withdrawCollateral(params, amount, ctx.self(), receiver);
  return { assets: amount, shares: 0 };
}

// `withdrawAmount`, `withdraw50Percent`, `withdrawAll` and `withdrawAmountOrAll`: an amount of
// assets, or a number of shares, never both.
function withdraw(id: Uint256, step: Uint256, amount: Uint256, receiver: Address): Moved {
  require(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const morpho = MorphoReads.at(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const params = morpho.idToMarketParams(id);
  morpho.accrueInterest(params);
  const supplyShares = morpho.position(id, ctx.self()).supplyShares;
  let assets = amount;
  let shares = 0;
  if (step == 5) {
    assets = 0;
    shares = supplyShares / 2;
  }
  if (step == 6) {
    assets = 0;
    shares = supplyShares;
  }
  if (step == 7) {
    const market = morpho.market(id);
    const assetsMax = toAssetsDown(
      supplyShares,
      market.totalSupplyAssets,
      market.totalSupplyShares,
    );
    if (amount >= assetsMax) {
      assets = 0;
      shares = supplyShares;
    }
  }
  const [withdrawn, burned] = MorphoBlue.Morpho.withdraw(
    params,
    assets,
    shares,
    ctx.self(),
    receiver,
  );
  return { assets: withdrawn, shares: burned };
}

function borrow(id: Uint256, amount: Uint256, receiver: Address): Moved {
  require(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const params = MorphoReads.at(MorphoBlue.Morpho).idToMarketParams(id);
  const [assets, shares] = MorphoBlue.Morpho.borrow(params, amount, 0, ctx.self(), receiver);
  return { assets: assets, shares: shares };
}

// `repayAmount`, `repay50Percent`, `repayAll` and `repayAmountOrAll`: by shares, the assets they
// cost are worked out as Morpho works them out, rounded up, and approved exactly.
function repay(id: Uint256, step: Uint256, amount: Uint256): Moved {
  require(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const morpho = MorphoReads.at(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const params = morpho.idToMarketParams(id);
  morpho.accrueInterest(params);
  const market = morpho.market(id);
  const borrowShares = morpho.position(id, ctx.self()).borrowShares;
  let assets = amount;
  let shares = 0;
  if (step == 10) {
    shares = borrowShares / 2;
  }
  if (step == 11) {
    shares = borrowShares;
  }
  if (step == 12) {
    if (amount >= toAssetsUp(borrowShares, market.totalBorrowAssets, market.totalBorrowShares)) {
      shares = borrowShares;
    }
  }
  if (shares > 0) {
    assets = toAssetsUp(shares, market.totalBorrowAssets, market.totalBorrowShares);
  }
  approve(params.loanToken, MorphoBlue.Morpho, assets);
  const [repaid, burned] = MorphoBlue.Morpho.repay(
    params,
    shares > 0 ? 0 : assets,
    shares,
    ctx.self(),
    hex``,
  );
  return { assets: repaid, shares: burned };
}

function main(step: Uint256, id: Uint256, amount: Uint256, receiver: Address): Snippet {
  require(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  require(step <= 12, "step is 0 to 12");
  let moved: Moved = { assets: 0, shares: 0 };
  if (step == 1) {
    moved = supply(id, amount);
  }
  if (step == 2) {
    moved = supplyCollateral(id, amount);
  }
  if (step == 3) {
    moved = withdrawCollateral(id, amount, receiver);
  }
  if (step >= 4 && step <= 7) {
    moved = withdraw(id, step, amount, receiver);
  }
  if (step == 8) {
    moved = borrow(id, amount, receiver);
  }
  if (step >= 9) {
    moved = repay(id, step, amount);
  }

  // The views, on the market with its interest accrued to now.
  const morpho = MorphoReads.at(MorphoBlue.Morpho);
  const params = morpho.idToMarketParams(id);
  morpho.accrueInterest(params);
  const market = morpho.market(id);
  const position = morpho.position(id, ctx.self());
  let borrowApy = 0;
  let supplyApy = 0;
  if (params.irm != 0) {
    borrowApy = wTaylorCompounded(MorphoReads.at(params.irm).borrowRateView(params, market), YEAR);
    const utilization =
      market.totalBorrowAssets == 0
        ? 0
        : (market.totalBorrowAssets * WAD + market.totalSupplyAssets - 1) /
          market.totalSupplyAssets;
    supplyApy = Math.mulDiv(Math.mulDiv(borrowApy, WAD - market.fee, WAD), utilization, WAD);
  }
  const borrowed = toAssetsUp(
    position.borrowShares,
    market.totalBorrowAssets,
    market.totalBorrowShares,
  );
  const collateralPrice = MorphoReads.at(params.oracle).price();
  const maxBorrow = Math.mulDiv(
    Math.mulDiv(position.collateral, collateralPrice, ORACLE_PRICE_SCALE),
    params.lltv,
    WAD,
  );
  return {
    assets: moved.assets,
    shares: moved.shares,
    supplyApy,
    borrowApy,
    supplied: toAssetsDown(
      position.supplyShares,
      market.totalSupplyAssets,
      market.totalSupplyShares,
    ),
    borrowed,
    collateral: position.collateral,
    totalSupply: market.totalSupplyAssets,
    totalBorrow: market.totalBorrowAssets,
    healthFactor: borrowed == 0 ? ~0 : (maxBorrow * WAD) / borrowed,
  };
}
```

## Pendle: the router samples

Ported from pendle-finance/pendle-examples-public, [`test/RouterSample.sol`](https://github.com/pendle-finance/pendle-examples-public/blob/642b1ab2784b3015691d6c26a2684cd5f7585b0d/test/RouterSample.sol): 265 lines of Solidity, 204 of them code. In Sauce, `pendle-router-sample.sauce.ts`: 226 lines, 172 of them code.

```ts
// Pendle's router samples, ported: `RouterSample` is Pendle's tour of its router, as tests that
// each spend 1 wstETH one way and turn what it bought back into wstETH: buy and sell PT, buy and
// sell YT, zap into a market's liquidity and out, mint and redeem SY, and mint and redeem PT with
// YT; and a zap that keeps the YT. Here `step` picks one, spending `amount` of `token` (one the
// market's SY takes), and returns what the first leg bought and what the second paid back, which
// must be at least `minBack`.
//
// Ported from pendle-finance/pendle-examples-public, test/RouterSample.sol (265 lines, 204 of code):
// https://github.com/pendle-finance/pendle-examples-public/blob/642b1ab2784b3015691d6c26a2684cd5f7585b0d/test/RouterSample.sol
//
// What changes in Sauce: the samples are tests on a fork, with `deal` for their wstETH and every
// token approved to the router for the maximum; the Pot spends its own `token` and approves each
// call for what it spends. Their market was a constant; `market` is an input. Their minimums were
// 0; `minBack` bounds the round trip. The YT sample sells the YT the router reports, a hair less
// than it delivers; the program sells what arrived. Their StructGen helpers are the functions
// below. Three samples are left out: the rewards one warps time on a fork; the one that batches
// two router calls through the router's own batching, which a program makes one after the other;
// and the try/catch claim, which probes a token's kind. The router functions the registry's ABI leaves out, and the market's
// `readTokens`, are in PendleRouterSample.json beside this file.
//
//   sauce run pendle-router-sample.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <step> <market> <token> <amount> <minBack>
//
//   step: Uint256       1 buy and sell PT, 2 buy and sell YT, 3 zap in and out, 4 mint and redeem
//                       SY, 5 mint and redeem PT and YT, 6 zap in keeping the YT
//   market: Address     the Pendle market, before its expiry
//   token: Address      the token spent and paid back: one its SY takes in and pays out
//   amount: Uint256     how much `token`, in its smallest units:
//                       1000000000000000000 is 1 wstETH (18 decimals)
//   minBack: Uint256    the least `token` the second leg must pay back (step 6: the least LP)
//
// On Ethereum, 1 wstETH through PT and back, on the wstETH market:
//
//   sauce run pendle-router-sample.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args 1 <market> 0x7f39C581F595B53c5cb19bD0b3f8dA6c935E2Ca0 1000000000000000000 <minBack>
import PendleRouterSample from "./PendleRouterSample.json";

interface Legs {
  out: Uint256;
  back: Uint256;
}

// StructGen's helpers: the router searches the trade's size on chain within `defaultApprox`'s
// bounds, and no aggregator swap and no limit order is used. Each returns a record the compiler
// builds where it is used.
function defaultApprox() {
  return { guessMin: 0, guessMax: ~0, guessOffchain: 0, maxIteration: 256, eps: 10 ** 14 };
}

function noSwap() {
  return { swapType: 0, extRouter: 0, extCalldata: hex``, needScale: false };
}

function createTokenInputStruct(tokenIn: Address, netTokenIn: Uint256) {
  return { tokenIn, netTokenIn, tokenMintSy: tokenIn, pendleSwap: 0, swapData: noSwap() };
}

function createTokenOutputStruct(tokenOut: Address, minTokenOut: Uint256) {
  return { tokenOut, minTokenOut, tokenRedeemSy: tokenOut, pendleSwap: 0, swapData: noSwap() };
}

function emptyLimit() {
  return { limitRouter: 0, epsSkipMarket: 0, normalFills: [], flashFills: [], optData: hex`` };
}

function buyAndSellPt(market: Address, token: Address, amount: Uint256, minBack: Uint256): Legs {
  require(Pendle.Router);
  const router = PendleRouterSample.at(Pendle.Router);
  const [, pt] = PendleRouterSample.at(market).readTokens();
  approve(token, Pendle.Router, amount);
  const [netPtOut] = Pendle.Router.swapExactTokenForPt(
    ctx.self(),
    market,
    0,
    defaultApprox(),
    createTokenInputStruct(token, amount),
    emptyLimit(),
  );
  approve(pt, Pendle.Router, netPtOut);
  const [netTokenOut] = router.swapExactPtForToken(
    ctx.self(),
    market,
    netPtOut,
    createTokenOutputStruct(token, minBack),
    emptyLimit(),
  );
  return { out: netPtOut, back: netTokenOut };
}

function buyAndSellYt(market: Address, token: Address, amount: Uint256, minBack: Uint256): Legs {
  require(Pendle.Router);
  const router = PendleRouterSample.at(Pendle.Router);
  const [, , yt] = PendleRouterSample.at(market).readTokens();
  const ytBefore = Token(yt).balanceOf(ctx.self());
  approve(token, Pendle.Router, amount);
  Pendle.Router.swapExactTokenForYt(
    ctx.self(),
    market,
    0,
    defaultApprox(),
    createTokenInputStruct(token, amount),
    emptyLimit(),
  );
  // The router reports a hair less YT than it delivers; selling what arrived leaves none behind.
  const netYtOut = Token(yt).balanceOf(ctx.self()) - ytBefore;
  approve(yt, Pendle.Router, netYtOut);
  const [netTokenOut] = router.swapExactYtForToken(
    ctx.self(),
    market,
    netYtOut,
    createTokenOutputStruct(token, minBack),
    emptyLimit(),
  );
  return { out: netYtOut, back: netTokenOut };
}

function zapInAndZapOut(market: Address, token: Address, amount: Uint256, minBack: Uint256): Legs {
  require(Pendle.Router);
  approve(token, Pendle.Router, amount);
  const [netLpOut] = Pendle.Router.addLiquiditySingleToken(
    ctx.self(),
    market,
    0,
    defaultApprox(),
    createTokenInputStruct(token, amount),
    emptyLimit(),
  );
  approve(market, Pendle.Router, netLpOut);
  const [netTokenOut] = Pendle.Router.removeLiquiditySingleToken(
    ctx.self(),
    market,
    netLpOut,
    createTokenOutputStruct(token, minBack),
    emptyLimit(),
  );
  return { out: netLpOut, back: netTokenOut };
}

function mintRedeemSy(market: Address, token: Address, amount: Uint256, minBack: Uint256): Legs {
  require(Pendle.Router);
  const router = PendleRouterSample.at(Pendle.Router);
  const [sy] = PendleRouterSample.at(market).readTokens();
  approve(token, Pendle.Router, amount);
  const netSyOut = router.mintSyFromToken(ctx.self(), sy, 0, createTokenInputStruct(token, amount));
  approve(sy, Pendle.Router, netSyOut);
  const netTokenOut = router.redeemSyToToken(
    ctx.self(),
    sy,
    netSyOut,
    createTokenOutputStruct(token, minBack),
  );
  return { out: netSyOut, back: netTokenOut };
}

function mintRedeemPtAndYt(
  market: Address,
  token: Address,
  amount: Uint256,
  minBack: Uint256,
): Legs {
  require(Pendle.Router);
  const router = PendleRouterSample.at(Pendle.Router);
  const [, pt, yt] = PendleRouterSample.at(market).readTokens();
  approve(token, Pendle.Router, amount);
  const [netPyOut] = router.mintPyFromToken(
    ctx.self(),
    yt,
    0,
    createTokenInputStruct(token, amount),
  );
  // Redeeming burns an equal amount of PT and YT.
  approve(pt, Pendle.Router, netPyOut);
  approve(yt, Pendle.Router, netPyOut);
  const [netTokenOut] = router.redeemPyToToken(
    ctx.self(),
    yt,
    netPyOut,
    createTokenOutputStruct(token, minBack),
  );
  return { out: netPyOut, back: netTokenOut };
}

// The zap with no price impact: the YT it mints along the way is kept, and the LP is all it adds.
function zeroPriceImpactZap(
  market: Address,
  token: Address,
  amount: Uint256,
  minLpOut: Uint256,
): Legs {
  require(Pendle.Router);
  approve(token, Pendle.Router, amount);
  const [netLpOut, netYtOut] = PendleRouterSample.at(Pendle.Router).addLiquiditySingleTokenKeepYt(
    ctx.self(),
    market,
    minLpOut,
    0,
    createTokenInputStruct(token, amount),
  );
  return { out: netLpOut, back: netYtOut };
}

function main(
  step: Uint256,
  market: Address,
  token: Address,
  amount: Uint256,
  minBack: Uint256,
): Legs {
  if (step == 1) {
    return buyAndSellPt(market, token, amount, minBack);
  }
  if (step == 2) {
    return buyAndSellYt(market, token, amount, minBack);
  }
  if (step == 3) {
    return zapInAndZapOut(market, token, amount, minBack);
  }
  if (step == 4) {
    return mintRedeemSy(market, token, amount, minBack);
  }
  if (step == 5) {
    return mintRedeemPtAndYt(market, token, amount, minBack);
  }
  require(step == 6, "step is 1 to 6");
  return zeroPriceImpactZap(market, token, amount, minBack);
}
```

## Uniswap V4: the swap guide

Ported from Uniswap/docs, [`content/protocols/v4/guides/swapping/swapping.mdx`](https://github.com/Uniswap/docs/blob/338d70983ac49911aecac02dd57b0a969c1ca61e/content/protocols/v4/guides/swapping/swapping.mdx): 79 lines of Solidity, 61 of them code. In Sauce, `uniswap-v4-swap.sauce.ts`: 80 lines, 42 of them code.

```ts
// Uniswap's V4 swap guide, ported: its `Example` contract approves the Universal Router through
// Permit2, then sells `amountIn` of a V4 pool's `currency0` for its `currency1` with one `V4_SWAP`
// command: a single-pool exact-input swap, its input settled and its output taken. It returns the
// `currency1` the swap delivered, and fails below `minAmountOut`.
//
// Ported from Uniswap/docs, content/protocols/v4/guides/swapping/swapping.mdx (79 lines, 61 of code):
// https://github.com/Uniswap/docs/blob/338d70983ac49911aecac02dd57b0a969c1ca61e/content/protocols/v4/guides/swapping/swapping.mdx
//
// What changes in Sauce: the contract was deployed with the router's, the pool manager's and
// Permit2's addresses; the program names them `UniswapV4.UniversalRouter` and `Permit2.Permit2`.
// The guide's two functions run in one cook, `approveTokenWithPermit2` first: it approved Permit2
// for the maximum, and the program approves Permit2 for `amountIn` alone. Its output was the
// contract's whole balance of `currency1`; the program measures what the swap added. The guide's
// count is its contract: its setup, its approval and its complete swap function.
//
//   sauce run uniswap-v4-swap.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <key> <amountIn> <minAmountOut>
//
//   key: { currency0: Address, currency1: Address, fee: Uint256, tickSpacing: Uint256, hooks: Address }
//                           the pool, as V4 keys it: its two tokens in address order, its fee in
//                           millionths, its tick spacing and its hooks (0 for none)
//   amountIn: Uint256       the `currency0` to sell, in its smallest units: 1000000000 is 1,000 USDC
//   minAmountOut: Uint256   the least `currency1` to accept, in its smallest units
//
// On Ethereum, 1,000 USDC sold for at least 0.25 WETH in the 0.05% USDC/WETH pool, which has no
// hooks:
//
//   sauce run uniswap-v4-swap.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args '{"currency0":"0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48","currency1":"0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2","fee":500,"tickSpacing":10,"hooks":"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"}' \
//     1000000000 250000000000000000

// The Universal Router's command, and the V4 router's actions, as the libraries number them.
const V4_SWAP = hex`10`;
const SWAP_EXACT_IN_SINGLE = hex`06`;
const SETTLE_ALL = hex`0c`;
const TAKE_ALL = hex`0f`;

interface PoolKey {
  currency0: Address;
  currency1: Address;
  fee: Uint256;
  tickSpacing: Uint256;
  hooks: Address;
}

function approveTokenWithPermit2(token: Address, amount: Uint256, expiration: Uint256): void {
  require(Permit2.Permit2 && UniswapV4.UniversalRouter);
  approve(token, Permit2.Permit2, amount);
  Permit2.Permit2.approve(token, UniswapV4.UniversalRouter, amount, expiration);
}

function swapExactInputSingle(key: PoolKey, amountIn: Uint256, minAmountOut: Uint256): Uint256 {
  require(UniswapV4.UniversalRouter);
  const actions = SWAP_EXACT_IN_SINGLE.concat(SETTLE_ALL, TAKE_ALL);
  // Solidity encodes one struct that holds bytes as one value, behind an offset; `abi.encode`
  // encodes a record as its fields, so the struct goes in a record of its own.
  const params = [
    abi.encode({
      exactInputSingle: {
        poolKey: key,
        zeroForOne: true,
        amountIn,
        amountOutMinimum: minAmountOut,
        hookData: hex``,
      },
    }),
    abi.encode(key.currency0, amountIn),
    abi.encode(key.currency1, minAmountOut),
  ];
  const before = Token(key.currency1).balanceOf(ctx.self());
  UniswapV4.UniversalRouter.execute(V4_SWAP, [abi.encode(actions, params)], ctx.timestamp() + 20);
  const amountOut = Token(key.currency1).balanceOf(ctx.self()) - before;
  require(amountOut >= minAmountOut, "Insufficient output amount");
  return amountOut;
}

function main(key: PoolKey, amountIn: Uint256, minAmountOut: Uint256): Uint256 {
  approveTokenWithPermit2(key.currency0, amountIn, ctx.timestamp());
  return swapExactInputSingle(key, amountIn, minAmountOut);
}
```

## Balancer V2: batch swaps

Ported from balancer/docs, [`docs/reference/swaps/batch-swaps.md`](https://github.com/balancer/docs/blob/bc51cd265e21152ff22e59c7ffac50d3529db25c/docs/reference/swaps/batch-swaps.md): 30 lines of Solidity, 30 of them code. In Sauce, `balancer-v2-batch-swap.sauce.ts`: 101 lines, 56 of them code.

```ts
// Balancer's batch swap examples, ported: Balancer's batch swap guide routes token A to token C
// through B, across two pools, in one call to the Vault's `batchSwap`: "given in" sells exactly
// `amount` of A, its first step taking `amount` and its second the first's whole output (an amount
// of 0); "given out" buys exactly `amount` of C, its steps running backwards from C. `limit` bounds
// the other side, as the guide's limits do: the least C, or the most A. It returns what the Pot
// paid in A and what `recipient` received in C.
//
// Ported from balancer/docs, docs/reference/swaps/batch-swaps.md (30 lines, 30 of code):
// https://github.com/balancer/docs/blob/bc51cd265e21152ff22e59c7ffac50d3529db25c/docs/reference/swaps/batch-swaps.md
//
// What changes in Sauce: the guide gives `batchSwap`'s interface and its two multi-hop examples as
// tables, not a contract; the program is those examples, through `BalancerV2.Vault`. The Pot is
// the sender and pays from its own balance; `recipient` receives. The guide's warning holds: limits
// computed on chain by `queryBatchSwap` in the same transaction can be sandwiched, so `limit` is a
// `main` input, worked out before the transaction. Its count is the guide's code: the interface
// and its structs.
//
//   sauce run balancer-v2-batch-swap.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <givenOut> <poolAB> <poolBC> <a> <b> <c> <amount> <limit> <recipient>
//
//   givenOut: bool       false: sell exactly `amount` of A; true: buy exactly `amount` of C
//   poolAB: Uint256      the id of the pool that trades A and B, as the Vault names it
//   poolBC: Uint256      the id of the pool that trades B and C
//   a: Address           the token paid
//   b: Address           the token between
//   c: Address           the token received
//   amount: Uint256      the A to sell, or the C to buy, in its smallest units:
//                        1000000000 is 1,000 USDC (6 decimals)
//   limit: Uint256       the least C to accept, or with `givenOut` the most A to pay
//   recipient: Address   who receives the C
//
// On Ethereum, 1,000 USDC sold for WBTC through WETH, in the 50/50 USDC/WETH and WBTC/WETH pools:
//
//   sauce run balancer-v2-batch-swap.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args false 0x96646936b91d6b9d7d0c47c496afbf3d6ec7b6f8000200000000000000000019 \
//     0xa6f548df93de924d73be7d25dc02554c6bd66db500020000000000000000000e \
//     0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 \
//     <wbtc> 1000000000 <limit> <recipient>

const GIVEN_IN = 0;
const GIVEN_OUT = 1;

interface Swapped {
  paid: Uint256;
  received: Uint256;
}

function main(
  givenOut: bool,
  poolAB: Uint256,
  poolBC: Uint256,
  a: Address,
  b: Address,
  c: Address,
  amount: Uint256,
  limit: Uint256,
  recipient: Address,
): Swapped {
  require(BalancerV2.Vault);
  const maxIn = givenOut ? limit : amount;
  approve(a, BalancerV2.Vault, maxIn);
  // Example 1, given in: A → B, then all of that B → C. Example 2, given out: C ← B first, then
  // the B that costs ← A. The second step's amount is 0: the first step's result.
  const swaps = [
    {
      poolId: givenOut ? poolBC : poolAB,
      assetInIndex: givenOut ? 1 : 0,
      assetOutIndex: givenOut ? 2 : 1,
      amount,
      userData: hex``,
    },
    {
      poolId: givenOut ? poolAB : poolBC,
      assetInIndex: givenOut ? 0 : 1,
      assetOutIndex: givenOut ? 1 : 2,
      amount: 0,
      userData: hex``,
    },
  ];
  const funds = {
    sender: ctx.self(),
    fromInternalBalance: false,
    recipient,
    toInternalBalance: false,
  };
  // A limit is what the Vault may take of each asset: positive in, negative out.
  const limits = [maxIn, 0, givenOut ? -amount : -limit];
  const deltas = BalancerV2.Vault.batchSwap(
    givenOut ? GIVEN_OUT : GIVEN_IN,
    swaps,
    [a, b, c],
    funds,
    limits,
    ctx.timestamp(),
  );
  // What the Vault did not take of the allowance does not stand.
  if (deltas[0] < maxIn) {
    approve(a, BalancerV2.Vault, 0);
  }
  return { paid: deltas[0], received: -deltas[2] };
}
```

## Balancer V2: a flash swap

Ported from balancer/docs, [`docs/reference/swaps/flash-swaps.md`](https://github.com/balancer/docs/blob/bc51cd265e21152ff22e59c7ffac50d3529db25c/docs/reference/swaps/flash-swaps.md): 30 lines of Solidity, 30 of them code. In Sauce, `balancer-v2-flash-swap.sauce.ts`: 65 lines, 30 of them code.

```ts
// Balancer's flash swap, ported: when two Balancer pools price the same two tokens apart, one
// `batchSwap` sells `amount` of A to the first pool for B and sells all that B back to the second
// for A. The Vault settles the batch as a whole, so the Pot sends nothing: its limits are zero, and
// the A the second pool pays beyond `amount` goes to `recipient`. A cycle that would cost anything
// fails on those limits and reverts. It returns the profit.
//
// Ported from balancer/docs, docs/reference/swaps/flash-swaps.md (30 lines, 30 of code):
// https://github.com/balancer/docs/blob/bc51cd265e21152ff22e59c7ffac50d3529db25c/docs/reference/swaps/flash-swaps.md
//
// What changes in Sauce: nothing in how it works. A Balancer flash swap is the one flash loan with
// no callback: the Vault nets the steps before anyone pays, so the Pot needs no tokens and no
// Router. The guide shows the transaction's arguments, which the program builds; its count is that
// transaction's code.
//
//   sauce run balancer-v2-flash-swap.sauce.ts --chain <chain> --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <sellPool> <buyPool> <a> <b> <amount> <recipient>
//
//   sellPool: Uint256    the id of the pool A is sold to, where A is dear
//   buyPool: Uint256     the id of the pool A is bought back from, where A is cheap
//   a: Address           the token the cycle starts and ends with
//   b: Address           the token between
//   amount: Uint256      the A sold to the first pool, in its smallest units:
//                        1000000000000000000 is 1 WETH (18 decimals)
//   recipient: Address   who receives the profit, in A
//
// On Ethereum, 1 WETH around two pools of WETH and USDC, one of them Balancer's 50/50 pool:
//
//   sauce run balancer-v2-flash-swap.sauce.ts --chain ethereum --keystore <keystore> \
//     --args <sellPool> 0x96646936b91d6b9d7d0c47c496afbf3d6ec7b6f8000200000000000000000019 \
//     0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 \
//     1000000000000000000 <recipient>

const GIVEN_IN = 0;

function main(
  sellPool: Uint256,
  buyPool: Uint256,
  a: Address,
  b: Address,
  amount: Uint256,
  recipient: Address,
): Uint256 {
  require(BalancerV2.Vault);
  const swaps = [
    { poolId: sellPool, assetInIndex: 0, assetOutIndex: 1, amount, userData: hex`` },
    // An amount of 0 is the step before's whole output.
    { poolId: buyPool, assetInIndex: 1, assetOutIndex: 0, amount: 0, userData: hex`` },
  ];
  const funds = {
    sender: ctx.self(),
    fromInternalBalance: false,
    recipient,
    toInternalBalance: false,
  };
  // Zero limits: the Vault may take nothing of either token from the Pot.
  const deltas = BalancerV2.Vault.batchSwap(
    GIVEN_IN,
    swaps,
    [a, b],
    funds,
    [0, 0],
    ctx.timestamp(),
  );
  return -deltas[0];
}
```
